text.p: CS Research recommended overweighting the planned new pharmaceuticals concern Novartis in a model portfolio, according to a recent study.

CS analyst Christian Prinz said Ciba Geigy AG and Sandoz AG, the two Swiss firms which plan to merge to form the pharmaceutical giant Novartis, have shown higher than expected sales in the first half of 1996.

The study said that Sandoz's sales were fueled by growth in the pharmaceuticals sector. Its net profit in the first half was up 12 percent, with operating income also fueled by agribusiness. For the full year, CS expected Sandoz's operating profit to reach 2.93 billion Swiss francs, a gain of eight percent.
The study said Ciba's sales were also above expectations, with the agriculture division posting strongest growth.
But it noted that Ciba's net profit growth was below expectations. It said that operating profit was burdened by a weak performance in its industry division.
This included a difficult environment for textile dyes.

But it said that an improvement seen in that sector in the second quarter appeared to be continuing in the third quarter. For the full year, operating profit was expected to reach 3.22 billion Swiss francs, a gain of 5.7 percent. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
